disposition_reason: Tables 1 and 2 print mean arsenic, lead and cadmium in market beef muscle, liver and kidney from three Accra markets.

study.design: Cross-sectional market survey, 10 randomly selected vendors per market, three tissues
study.origin: not stated (cattle from abattoirs supplying the markets)
study.market: Ashaiman Main, Madina and Makola markets, Accra Metropolis, Ghana
study.method: 3 g fresh tissue digested with HNO3 and H2SO4, made up to 50 mL; graphite tube atomizer AAS (GTA 120, 200 Series AA)
study.qa: Two analytical replicates per sample; no CRM, recovery or blank results reported

findings.material_label: Beef (muscle, liver and kidney; market means)
findings.integrity_flag: Unit conflict: table unit mg/100g implies about 2-25 mg/kg, but the text compares the same numbers with a 1 mg/kg lead limit and says no sample exceeded it; the true unit cannot be resolved, so no µg/kg value is stored
findings.notes: Market mean across tissues as interpreted (10 vendors x 3 tissues per market); text describes some of these values as muscle. SEM 0.162 mg/100g. Two analytical replicates per sample.

unresolved: Unit conflict: tables print mg/100g, but the discussion compares the same numbers with 1 mg/kg limits (and says none exceeded the lead limit), which only fits if the unit were mg/kg or smaller. Values kept verbatim without conversion.
Table 1 does not say whether market means pool all three tissues; the text calls Table 1 values muscle values, but Table 2 gives different muscle means.
The abstract says the liver had comparatively lower metal concentrations and recommends it, contradicting Table 2 where liver is highest for all three metals.
Lead and arsenic wavelengths (271.0 and 197.2 nm) are unusual; no detection limits or reference materials are reported.
